72.0.s.en: (1) Characteristics of the kingdom of God

72.0.0.en: 1- Give the king thy judgments, O God, and thy righteousness unto the king's son.

72.0.1.en: 1- The writer of the Psalm, who is Solomon, or David, asks for the king and the king's son at the same time, and this applies to Solomon, and not to David or Saul who preceded him. And he asks for him two things:

72.0.2.en: a- "Thy judgments", that is, wisdom, because of Solomon's young age, and God praised this request because he did not ask for riches, or power over enemies, but asked for something that benefits him and his people spiritually and administratively.

72.0.3.en: b- "Thy righteousness", and what is meant by righteousness is justice and goodness, that he may be saved and live with God, and be an example to his people.

72.0.4.en: 2- This verse also applies to Christ, who is the king's son, because He is of the offspring of David. For Christ is the hypostasis of Wisdom, and in Him is the perfection of justice.

72.1.0.en: 2- He shall judge thy people with righteousness, and thy poor with judgment.

72.1.1.en: 1- From this verse the writer of the Psalm begins to list the characteristics of the king, meaning King Solomon, or Christ. The first two characteristics are justice and truth, for he uses them in his rule over his people. This people is the Jews, who are characterized by humility before God, and therefore he calls them the poor, that is, the poor in spirit.

72.1.2.en: 2- The king judges his people, who are the Jews, and also the poor, and these may be meant to be the Gentiles, that is, he rules the Jews and the Gentiles with justice and truth. This is a prophecy about Christ, in whom the Gentiles believe, so He judges and rules the whole world, that is, all people who have believed in Him, whether from the Jews or the Gentiles.

72.2.0.en: 3- The mountains shall bring peace to the people, and the little hills, by righteousness.

72.2.1.en: 1- The third and fourth characteristics are peace and righteousness. By the mountains that bring peace are meant the spiritually great, whose lives are lofty like high mountains. These are full of peace, and at the same time an example to the rest of the people. As for the little hills, they are also the spiritual people who are lower in rank than the mountains. These are full of righteousness and goodness, and they too are an example to others. The meaning of this is that the reign of Solomon was a reign of peace, and gave the spiritual people an opportunity to live with God and to be elevated in their lives.

72.2.2.en: 2- This verse also applies to Christ, who is the God of peace, and gave peace to His disciples and His people, and likewise is the Righteous and Holy One, who said, "Which of you convinceth me of sin?"

72.2.4.en: 3- The mountains also symbolize the angels and the saints in heaven, who are the Church Triumphant, while the little hills symbolize the saints living on earth, that is, the Church Militant.

72.3.0.en: 4- He shall judge the poor of the people, he shall save the children of the needy, and shall break in pieces the oppressor.

72.3.1.en: 1- The fifth characteristic of the king is that he is a judge, so he gives justice to the wronged and punishes the oppressor. So he saves the poor and the needy, that is, the weak and the helpless, and at the same time he punishes the oppressor by breaking him in pieces, that is, destroying his power and his domination over the poor.

72.3.2.en: 2- The poor and the needy are the humble; these Christ saves by His blood on the Cross, while the oppressor, who is Satan, He breaks in pieces by binding him, and after this, on the Day of Judgment, He casts him into eternal torment.

72.4.0.en: 5- They shall fear thee as long as the sun and moon endure, throughout all generations.

72.4.1.en: 1- The sixth characteristic of the king is fear, that is, his people fear him, revere him and respect him. Solomon had great awe because of his power and his justice and his keen intelligence. He managed the country in the best way, and no one could stand before him; even his opponents fled, or were bound and unable to overcome him. And what is meant by the sun and the moon is day and night, that is, all through the night.

72.4.2.en: 2- This verse applies to Christ more than to Solomon, for He is the Sun of Righteousness rising upon His Church, which is the moon, and the fear of Him is in the hearts of all because of His authority, for He spoke with authority and not as the scribes and Pharisees (Mt 7:29). In addition, the fear of Him and His kingdom endure throughout all generations, that is, forever, as the angel declared to the Virgin Lady (Lk 1:32).

72.5.0.en: 6- He shall come down like rain upon the mown grass: as showers that water the earth.

72.5.1.en: Fleeces (jazaz): plural of fleece (jazza), which is a piece of wool taken from sheep.

72.5.2.en: Showers (ghuyuth): plural of ghayth, which is rain.

72.5.3.en: Watering (dharifa): that which flows and runs.

72.5.4.en: 1- The seventh characteristic of the king is spiritual consolation. Solomon was successful in managing his country, and he had authority, so the surrounding nations feared him, and not only his people but also his neighbors cooperated with him. So his country became rich, so much so that the Holy Bible declared that gold and silver were like stones in Jerusalem (2 Chr 1:15). So he poured out good upon the fleece, that is, Jerusalem, and also upon the earth, which is all the land of the children of Israel.

72.5.5.en: 2- By the redemption of Christ He gave salvation to everyone who believes in Him from the whole world, so He poured out the blessings of salvation by the Holy Spirit upon the fleece, who are the Jews who became Christians, and upon the earth, which is the Gentiles who believed in Him.

72.5.6.en: 3- The fleece is the Virgin who received the glad tidings of the divine conception for the salvation of the world, and the earth is the whole world which received the good news of salvation by means of the showers, who are the Apostles, the priests and the servants.

72.6.0.en: 7- In his days shall the righteous flourish; and abundance of peace so long as the moon endureth.

72.6.2.en: 1- The eighth characteristic of the king is that he is the giver of joy; because the days of Solomon were peace, they gave the righteous an opportunity to grow spiritually, so they enjoyed fellowship with God, and remained occupied with God, worshiping Him in His Temple and clinging to Him until the moon passed away, which is Solomon, that is, until the end of Solomon's life.

72.6.3.en: 2- And when we apply this verse to Christ, it means that the righteous grow strongly in the New Testament because of the blessings of salvation which they receive through Christ, and they rejoice, indeed they shine upon others and are a light for the world, as Christ commanded them, and the righteous remain shining throughout the life of the Church on earth, which is symbolized by the moon.

72.6.4.en: Enjoy the characteristics of the kingdom of God in His Church, and care about attending the Church and receiving her sacraments, so that you live with the heavenly saints while you are on earth, and rejoice at all times in Christ who dwells in you.

72.7.s.en: (2) The extent of the kingdom of God

72.7.0.en: 8- He shall have dominion also from sea to sea, and from the river unto the ends of the earth.

72.7.1.en: 1- The ninth characteristic of the king is that he has great authority. God granted Solomon to be the greatest of the kings of his age, and his kingdom extended from sea to sea, and from the river to the ends of the earth, that is, his kingdom was very wide, for the kingdom of the children of Israel reached its widest extent in the days of David and Solomon. Perhaps what is meant by from sea to sea is from the Mediterranean Sea in the west to the Red Sea in the south, and perhaps what is meant by the river is the river Euphrates, and to the ends of the earth, that is, a vast extent of Solomon's kingdom because God blessed him.

72.7.2.en: 2- And if we apply this verse to Christ, what is meant is that He is the King of kings who reigned over the whole earth; for many from the different peoples of the earth believed in Him (Acts 4:4).

72.8.0.en: 9- They that dwell in the wilderness shall bow before him; and his enemies shall lick the dust. 10- The kings of Tarshish and of the isles shall bring presents: the kings of Sheba and Seba shall offer gifts. 11- Yea, all kings shall fall down before him: all nations shall serve him. Bow (tajthu): kneel and prostrate. Tarshish: an important commercial city in the south of Spain, and it is the last famous commercial center in the ancient world, since it lies in the far west of the world.

72.8.1.en: Sheba and Seba: countries lying in the south of the Arabian peninsula.

72.8.2.en: 1- King Solomon became so great that the nations around him submitted to him, and tried to appease him by presenting him with gifts; for he was strong, and rich by the blessing of God, so that the kings feared him. And the queen of Sheba came with many gifts, and marveled when she saw his great glory, while those who tried to stand against him were unable to resist him, and submitted to him, as the verse (v. 9) expresses it, that they lick the dust, that is, his authority extended over the whole earth by the submission of the kings to him.

72.8.3.en: 2- This verse clearly applies to Christ, who is the King of kings, and the kings of the earth and its rulers submitted to Him, such as the Magi, who came from the East and worshiped Him and presented gifts, and many of the rulers and kings of the earth submitted to Him by faith.

72.8.4.en: If you hold fast to God's commandments, He gives you awe in the eyes of those around you, and they see God in you and so submit to you, that is, they respect you and learn from you without your knowing it, so do not give up your great position by submitting to the lusts of the world, and be always a light to the world.

72.9.0.en: 12- For he shall deliver the needy when he crieth; the poor also, and him that hath no helper.

72.9.1.en: 1- The writer of the Psalm shows the characteristics of the loving king, and makes clear his love for his people through many characteristics, the first of which is the deliverer. He cares for the poor and for their cries to him, so he provides for them and delivers them from all the effects of poverty, such as the feeling of deprivation. And he protects them from falling into theft, murmuring and rebellion, and so gives them peace.

72.9.2.en: 2- And the second characteristic of the king is that he is the helper of the weak and the poor, so he supports them in all their spiritual, psychological and bodily needs.

72.9.3.en: These are the characteristics of King Solomon to a great extent, but their perfection appears in Christ the King of kings, who cared for and supported everyone in need, especially those who have no one, like the sick man at the pool of Bethesda (Jn 5:1-15).

72.10.0.en: 13- He shall spare the poor and needy, and shall save the souls of the needy.

72.10.1.en: 1- The third characteristic of the loving king is compassion for the poor and the needy. His heart is full of tenderness, and he not only helps them, but is gentle with them and patient with them, as a mother bends over her nursing child, and in this he encourages them and gladdens their hearts.

72.10.2.en: 2- The fourth characteristic of the loving king is that he is the savior, so he saves the poor from poverty, and satisfies them, and also from its effects in their lives, so that they live reassured, with strong spirits, and thankful to God.

72.11.0.en: 14- He shall redeem their soul from deceit and violence: and precious shall their blood be in his sight.

72.11.1.en: 1- The fifth characteristic of the loving king is that he is the Redeemer, who redeems his people from injustice and the greed of others toward them, who snatch away their small possessions. This is because the king is just, strong and able to protect his weak people. And this characteristic is perfected in Christ, who redeemed His people by His death for them on the Cross and by giving them new life in Him, and delivered them from the oppressor, who is Satan.

72.11.2.en: 2- The sixth characteristic of the loving king is that he honors those who endured hardships and afflictions, and died unjustly, so he cares for their bodies and their tombs, and shows their righteousness and goodness. And the greatness of this characteristic appears in Christ, who honors the bodies of His saints, making some of them not decay, and encourages His people to hold their feasts and hymns of praise, and to name His churches after their names.

72.11.3.en: I wish you would show your love for those around you, especially the needy, the weak and the helpless, and not be content with helping them, for your smile and your kind words are what they need most. And those in need of the kind word may be the people of your own household, so do not forget them.

72.12.0.en: 15- And he shall live, and to him shall be given of the gold of Sheba: prayer also shall be made for him continually; and daily shall he be praised.

72.12.1.en: 1- Here he speaks of God's blessings to the king, so He grants him to live and have life, and this is a greeting offered to the king even until now: "Long live the king."

72.12.2.en: 2- And God enriches the king, so the people present to him precious offerings, such as the pure gold taken from the land of Sheba. Solomon became very rich, and became the richest of the kings of his age. And gold symbolizes heavenly life, that is, the people presented to him not only material gifts, but their hearts and their lives which live by God's commandments, and so became exalted.

72.12.3.en: 3- Likewise the people loved King Solomon, so they prayed for him continually because of his great characteristics mentioned above, and this gladdens the heart of God, that the king loves his people, and the people love the king, and pray for him.

72.12.4.en: 4- God gives the king a constant blessing all his life, so that everything he does prospers. Solomon's trade and works and his relations with the surrounding nations prospered.

72.12.5.en: 5- When we apply this verse to Christ we find that He is the One who lives forever, and the Magi presented gifts to Him: gold, frankincense and myrrh. And the Father showed His love and His blessing to the Son, so that those who believe in Christ pray in His name continually, and bless Him.

72.13.0.en: 16- There shall be an handful of corn in the earth upon the top of the mountains; the fruit thereof shall shake like Lebanon: and they of the city shall flourish like grass of the earth.

72.13.1.en: Handful (hufna): the fullness of the palm.

72.13.3.en: 1- The writer of the Psalm shows God's blessing with His children, for they are like a handful of grains of wheat cast on the mountains, which grow and yield ears even on the tops of the mountains where it is hard to farm because of the strength of the wind, and the harvest is plentiful like the trees of Lebanon filled with fruit, swaying with the winds, and the fruits are many in the city and in the field and everywhere, that is, God's blessing includes all the possessions of His children, who labored to prepare them, and everything is blessed by God.

72.13.4.en: 2- This verse applies to the Church, which is the grain of wheat, or the grain of mustard seed, which grew and became a great tree (Mt 13:32), and it came to have fruits everywhere, in the city and on the mountain by the grace of God, although it began small, but Christianity spread throughout the whole world in the first century.

72.14.0.en: 17- His name shall endure for ever: his name shall be continued as long as the sun: and men shall be blessed in him: all nations shall call him blessed.

72.14.1.en: 1- God's blessing to the king also appears in that his name remains forever, that is, the immortality of Solomon's soul forever in the Kingdom, because of his goodness. And also the news of his greatness spreads throughout the whole earth in his days, that is, wherever the sun rises and shines. In addition to this, King Solomon becomes a cause of blessing to everyone who deals with him. And in the end everyone who knows him blesses him, and magnifies him, and glorifies him.

72.14.2.en: 2- This verse clearly applies to Christ, whose name from eternity to eternity is great, and extends over the whole earth, and He is the source of blessing for the whole world. And in the end everyone blesses Him and glorifies Him.

72.15.0.en: . 18- Blessed be the Lord God, the God of Israel, who only doeth wondrous things.

72.15.1.en: At the end of the Psalm he declares that God deserves that we glorify Him, for He is blessed because of the great works He has done, whether in the creation of man, or with all mankind, or with His people the children of Israel. He is the only God, worthy of blessing, and not the gods of the pagan nations, which are demons.

72.16.0.en: . 19- And blessed be his glorious name for ever: and let the whole earth be filled with his glory; Amen, and Amen. The prayers of David the son of Jesse are ended.

72.16.1.en: 1- He closes the Psalm by giving glory to God forever, that is, to eternity, for He is glorified by His children on earth, and also by the heavenly ones, indeed the writer of the Psalm hopes that the earth will be filled with His glory, so that hearts and tongues are lifted up everywhere glorifying God. And this was indeed accomplished at the faith in Christ, for many of the Gentiles returned to God who created them, and glorified His holy name by their lives and by their lips.

72.16.2.en: 2- Many of the Fathers and commentators see that the last two verses of this Psalm (vv. 18, 19) are a glorification of God placed at the end of the second book of the Psalms according to the Jewish division, which is from (Ps 42) to (Ps 72), that is, these two verses are not part of Psalm 72, but a general conclusion of the second book.

72.16.3.en: 3- We see that (v. 19) ends with the word Amen, then Amen, as the rest of the books of the Psalms (the first, the third and the fourth) are concluded; as for the fifth, it is not written thus in it, because of the lack of need for it, since it is clear that it is the end of the whole Book of Psalms.

72.16.4.en: The blessing of the Lord is wonderful for His children, for it makes you need nothing of all that is in the world; it is enough for God to be with you, and you find that the little you have satisfies you and gladdens you, and if you need much He gives you. So hold fast to His commandments, and if you sin return quickly by repentance, and you will keep the blessing with you always.

72.16.5.en: God's dealings with the wicked and the righteous: "Truly God is good to Israel, even to such as are of a clean heart" (v. 1). Introduction:

72.16.6.en: 1- a- Its writer is Asaph, the chief of the singers in the days of David, and he is of the tribe of Levi, and he was assisted by two of the chiefs of the singers, Heman the Ezrahite and Ethan (who is also called Jeduthun) the Ezrahite (1 Chr 15:17). Asaph led the praise before the Ark of the Covenant in Jerusalem (1 Chr 16:4, 5, 7, 37), while Heman and Ethan led the praise before the Tabernacle at Gibeon (1 Chr 16:41).

72.16.7.en: b- There is an opinion that the writer of this Psalm is David, and he gave it to Asaph to sing. And Asaph was called the king's seer (1 Chr 25:5), (2 Chr 29:30, 35:15).

72.16.8.en: 2- When was it written? In the days of the prophet David, when Asaph was exposed to a personal trial in which he nearly fell into sin, but God rescued him from it, so his faith in God was established. This shows Asaph's courage in mentioning this matter about himself, like David his teacher who mentioned his fall into sin and his repentance.

72.16.9.en: 3- This Psalm may be a prophecy about a great trial that befell the people of God, namely the captivity, and then the return from it.

72.16.11.en: 5- This Psalm resembles Psalm 37 and Psalm 49 in speaking of the success of the wicked and the afflictions that meet the righteous, just as Job and Jeremiah were exposed to the same subject.

72.16.12.en: 6- The Psalm tells us of three important matters:

72.16.13.en: a- The success of the wicked is temporary.

72.16.14.en: b- Eternal destruction awaits the wicked.

72.16.15.en: c- The joy of the righteous in fellowship with God.

72.16.16.en: 7- With this Psalm begins the third book of the books of the Psalms according to the Jewish division, which ends with Psalm 89.

72.16.17.en: 8- Asaph cares about worship of the heart offered to God, and not outward worship, limited to offering sacrifices, and therefore he mentions the word heart six times in this Psalm.

72.16.18.en: 9- This Psalm is not found in the prayers of the Agpeya.
